newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas narrowly mixed late, still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas narrowly mixed late, still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained narrowly mixed late Tuesday in sluggish trade, with prices still stuck in narrow technical ranges amid little reason to move far in either direction, sources said.
At 1425 EDT, July eased 0.2 cent to $2.145 per million British thermal units, while August was 0.3 cent higher at $2.16. Other deferreds were still narrowly mixed.
"We're sliding sideways and I don't think there's any reason for the market to move much in either direction," said one Midwest trader, noting cash was still above the screen and mostly stable today.
While some said early news of a 20 mmcfd well blowout in Louisiana helped trigger some buying, they said enthusiasm was short-lived.
"The blowout was all hype. Until we get a big chunk of above-normal weather for five to seven days, we're not going to be able to rally much," a Houston trader said.
Chart watchers pegged the broad range in July between $2.055 and $2.21. Psychological support was seen at $2, with selling likely at $2.25 and $2.37.

Despite some heat in the Southwest this week, traders said the lack of load in most other regions offered little hope for a significant rally near-term. But some said forecasts for hotter weather later this week and next should limit any downside.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's AGA stock report range from 75 to 110 bcf versus a gain of 87 bcf a year ago.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas held steady in the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes gained a couple of cents to about the $2.05 level. New York city gate gas was flat on the day in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 16,533 contracts traded at 1355 EDT.
On the KCBT, July was still up by one-half cent at $2.015, while deferreds were steady to one-half cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.7 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
